threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still try to grab a seat on the bus. Locals know you have to be quick and just stand your ground.
Last night on the 322, a guy tried to sell his mixtape to everyone. By the time we hit Stockwell, he had a mini fan club.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One morning, I saw a guy in a full suit casually feeding pigeons while debating politics with a friend over coffee. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst and sit on a swingset made from repurposed bike parts while listening to a live punk band in a park.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know to never trust the BART schedule. If they suggest a backup plan, they're from here. Tourists just get frustrated.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy juggle on the bus while a grandma scolded him for interrupting her nap. Classic Muni—chaos wrapped in community.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for photo ops, but locals know they're the heartbeat of community life, especially during the evening jam sessions.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered looks at the metro signs, still holding tightly to their paper map like it's a treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still give way to cars at pedestrian crossings. The locals just walk out, and the taxis stop for them. It's a whole different game.
Last night on the 36, a woman in a bright yellow poncho danced down the aisle, singing old school R&B. We all clapped. Only in Peckham.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a busker playing old Kurdish songs while the kebab shop down the street was closing up. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can stumble upon hidden techno parties in abandoned buildings. It's the city's rebellious spirit alive and loud, a blast from the past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they roll their eyes at the BART delays while still ordering a burrito from the same spot since high school.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading the bus stop with a saxophone while a pigeon danced around him. Classic San Francisco hustle, you never know what you'll catch!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but miss the tiny bakeries tucked away in side streets, where the croissants are life-changing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they look for the metro sign every 100 meters; locals glide with confidence, while newcomers are still navigating the map.
